name: Fund for Investigative Journalism — Regular and Seed Grants (Summer cycle)
LMA AI Growth Lab (Local Media Association + Google)
what: Six-month AI implementation cohort for up to 12 local newsrooms, with Google training, coaching and capstone prototypes.
pitch: Eligibility is community-based, locally controlled outlets publishing original local journalism weekly — WPR exactly. Small orgs explicitly welcomed, peers matched by market size, and the prototype menu overlaps WPR's existing public-document tooling.
access: free (Google-funded, no stipend) · deadline Oct 14, 2026, 11:59pm ET · Nov–Apr program

name: CUNY Newmark AI Journalism Labs — 2027 Leaders and Creators tracks
what: Tuition-free 2027 cohort program where news leaders research an AI challenge over roughly fourteen weeks.
pitch: Microsoft covers tuition and a travel stipend for the mandatory New York kickoff, so cost to a two-person nonprofit is time only. Application asks for a specific AI challenge — WPR already has one running.
access: free (tuition-free, Microsoft Journalism funded; travel stipend) · deadline Oct 16, 2026

name: Report for America 2027–2028 host newsroom application
what: RFA places an early-career reporter in your newsroom and pays up to half the salary.
pitch: A third byline WPR cannot otherwise afford: RFA funds half a corps member's salary up to $27,500 and coaches the newsroom through local fundraising — directly useful to OEC's donor base, with nonprofits eligible.
access: free to apply · deadline Oct 19, 2026 · RFA pays half salary, up to $27,500

name: Tarbell Fellowship 2027–28 (Tarbell Center for AI Journalism)
what: Three-month AI journalism training plus a nine-month funded reporting placement covering artificial intelligence at a partner newsroom.
pitch: The only fully salaried AI journalism fellowship open right now. Placements run through Tarbell's partner newsrooms, so the realistic WPR play is both applying and asking to join the partner roster.
access: funded fellowship · deadline Nov 22, 2026 · $75,000–$120,000 salary ($115,000–$135,000 senior)

name: RJI Professional Innovation Fellowships (2027 class)
what: Remote fellowships paying individuals or organizations to build a free tool or resource for journalism.
pitch: The Emerging Technology track pays $100,000 to build exactly what OEC already does, and deliverables must end up free for any newsroom. Remote with only a couple of Columbia visits — survivable for a two-person shop.
access: free to apply · opens Nov 2, 2026, deadline Jan 8, 2027 · $75,000 individual/institutional, $100,000 emerging technology

name: Lenfest AI Collaborative and Fellowship Program — expanded cohort
what: Embedded AI engineering fellowships for news organizations, newly expanded with OpenAI money, credits and engineering support.
pitch: Announced Sept 28: $5M plus up to $5M in software credits, a wider range of news organizations invited, and an explicit push to turn fellowship projects into reusable shared tooling — OEC's exact thesis.
access: rolling letters of inquiry (no open call yet) · $5M fund plus up to $5M OpenAI credits
